Daily prices: Binance · recalculated about every 3 hours
Counts how many of about 20 large altcoins (e.g. Ethereum, Solana, XRP) have performed better than Bitcoin over the last 90 days. The value is their share from 0 to 100.
Prices: Binance or Bybit · reloaded about every 15 minutes

If dominance rises, Bitcoin is doing better than the rest of the market; if it falls, other coins gain weight. Stablecoins count too: if their value grows, the Bitcoin share drops even when the Bitcoin price stays the same.
Source: CoinGecko · reloaded about every 30 minutes
The share of Bitcoin in the total value of all cryptocurrencies (market capitalization). Below it is the share of Ethereum.
Below 25 means extreme fear, above 75 extreme greed, around 50 neutral. Expanded, the card shows the values from yesterday, a week ago and a month ago. Not a buy or sell signal.
Source: alternative.me · new value once a day
A sentiment index for the crypto market from 0 to 100. alternative.me calculates it from several inputs, including price swings, trading volume, social media and Bitcoin dominance.
Higher values mean the network is busy and transfers cost more. Slow, normal and fast are fees for a later or quicker confirmation. Expanded, the card shows the approximate cost of a simple transfer.
Public RPC nodes, mempool.space · reloaded every minute

What a transaction currently costs on each network. On Ethereum and similar networks in gwei (one billionth of an ETH per unit of gas), on Bitcoin in sat/vB (satoshis per virtual byte of the transaction).
Date: from block height and average block time (mempool.space), otherwise by calendar · price history: Coin Metrics, Binance, reloaded every 12 hours

At the halving, the reward miners receive for a new Bitcoin block is cut in half. This happens every 210,000 blocks, roughly every four years. After that, only half as many new bitcoins are created per day.
The note only appears when such a date is today or tomorrow. Around the release, prices often swing more than usual. The app shows only the date, not the figures themselves.
Calendar from the app website · loaded once a day
Dates of important US economic data: inflation (CPI, PCE), producer prices (PPI), the jobs report and interest rate decisions of the US Federal Reserve. Such figures often move crypto prices too.
Binance, Coin Metrics · prices hourly, on-chain values reloaded every 12 hours

The headline names the direction; expand the card for details. A broad move means most large coins are moving the same way. A high funding rate means many traders are betting on rising prices with leverage. A snapshot, not a forecast.
Binance, CoinGecko · reloaded about every 5 minutes

A short summary of the market over the last 24 hours: how Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana are moving, how many of the largest coins are rising or falling, how much Bitcoin is being traded right now and where the funding rate on Bitcoin futures stands.

On the right is the change in total value over 24 hours. High volume means a lot is being traded – it does not say in which direction. Shown in the conversion currency where possible, otherwise in US dollars.
All coins · CoinGecko · reloaded about every 30 minutes
The total value of all cryptocurrencies (market capitalization: price times circulating supply, added up over all coins) and the trading volume of the last 24 hours.
Each coin shows its most notable observation, with the 24-hour change on the right. A volume of 2× means twice the usual turnover. Unusual means neither good nor bad.
Binance, CoinGecko · reloaded about every 10 minutes

Up to five coins from the roughly 30 largest (without stablecoins) that are behaving unusually today: much stronger or weaker than Bitcoin, against the market direction, with unusually high trading volume or with a notable funding rate.
